====================================================================================================
TE RATE ATTRIBUTION — coefficient, driver, or the target's depth scope?
====================================================================================================

[A] THE MISS, restated  (1993-2026, n=33)
    steric target      0.12340 cm/yr
    Ladrillo L28 TE    0.15200 cm/yr   = 1.232x
    BRICK 2.0 TE       0.14458 cm/yr   = 1.172x   <= the SHARED miss

[B] THE DRIVER — FaIR's OHC against the observational products
    FaIR mean OHC (FULL-DEPTH)  1.3914 1e22 J/yr
    Zanna+Cheng (0-2000m)    1.0826 1e22 J/yr  n=33   FaIR/obs = 1.285
    Zanna+IGCC (0-2000m)     1.1258 1e22 J/yr  n=32   FaIR/obs = 1.236

[C] THE COEFFICIENT — alpha = rate(TE) / rate(OHC), model vs observations
    alpha model                     0.10925 cm per 1e22 J
    alpha implied by obs (Zanna+Cheng ) 0.11398   model/obs = 0.958
    alpha implied by obs (Zanna+IGCC  ) 0.10961   model/obs = 0.997
    => alpha is BELOW 1 in both arms (0.958-0.997): the coefficient is LOW
       and partially OFFSETS the driver. Tightening it would make the fit worse.

[D] THE DEPTH SCOPE — measured from IGCC's own >2000 m layer, not recalled
    IGCC 0-2000m        1.1258 1e22 J/yr
    IGCC FULL-DEPTH     1.2408 1e22 J/yr   => the >2000 m layer adds 10.2%
    FaIR / IGCC 0-2000m      1.215x   <= what the calibration target implies
    FaIR / IGCC FULL-DEPTH   1.102x   <= the LIKE-FOR-LIKE comparison
    => 52% of the apparent OHC overshoot is SCOPE, not error.

[E] IS THE TARGET ITSELF SCOPE-MIXED? — testing the splice's own assertion
    `prep_recalib_targets_ext.py:30` offset-matches Frederikse to NOAA as a 'pure
    level shift, no rescale -- both measure the same physical SLE'. On the overlap:
    NOAA 0-2000m thermosteric  0.12089 cm/yr  (n=14)
    target (= Frederikse here) 0.11330 cm/yr  (n=14)
    ratio Frederikse / NOAA    0.937
    ⚠ a level-matched splice does not equalise SLOPES. A ratio away from 1.00
      means the target's own two segments disagree on the trend, so the target
      changes scope/method at 2019 and a single 1993-2026 rate
      through it is a blend of both.


====================================================================================================
VERDICT
====================================================================================================
  NOT THE COEFFICIENT. alpha is 0.10925 cm per 1e22 J against the two obs-implied
  values -- 0.958-0.997x, i.e. slightly LOW and partially offsetting.
  IT IS THE DRIVER, AND ABOUT HALF OF THAT IS DEPTH SCOPE. FaIR is 1.21x the
  0-2000 m products the target is built from, but only 1.10x IGCC's OWN
  full-depth series. The >2000 m layer is 10% of the observed trend and
  FaIR includes it while the target does not.
  ⚠ THE RESIDUAL 1.10x IS A FaIR QUESTION, NOT A BRICK ONE -- which is exactly why
    BRICK 2.0 misses by the same amount. Nothing in either sea-level model can fix it.
  ⚠ AND THE CORRECTION IS AN UPPER BOUND. Scaling the steric target by the HEAT ratio
    1.102 overstates it: the deep ocean is colder, so its thermal expansion per
    joule is SMALLER than the upper ocean's. The true scope correction lies between
    1.00 and 1.102, so the model/target ratio lies between 1.12x and 1.23x.
  ⇒ THE FAIL SURVIVES AS A WARN AT WORST, AND IT IS NOT A SEA-LEVEL DEFECT.
